unharnessed.meaning: Every point survives: the sale, the old man's speech, finishing second, Doyle scouting, the Grand Rapids games, "Flynn misjuging that fly ball", the promise to come home. "it come as a shock" for "a surprise" is a fair shift.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "I'm not big-noting meself" for boasting, "running the eye over me", "having a squiz at me", "when I was on song" for when I was right, "not all up meself" for swelled up, "happy as Larry" for perfectly satisfied.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like a real Australian bush-league pitcher writing home: "Say g'day to all the boys", "nothing like that was on the cards", "never had a hope against me". The salutation "MATE AL" is a touch forced.
unharnessed.register: A steady middle weight, Jack's voice Aussie throughout without piling on; no swearing, within dad level.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps Jack's artless self-satisfied boasting while denying it: "you know I'm not big-noting meself when I say that Al".
unharnessed.flow: Reads like it was written that way, the original's run-on letter voice kept: "So I says I'd do me best and I thanked him for how I been treated in Terre Haute."
unharnessed.variety: Varied: "Fair dinkum", "on the cards", "guts", "big-noting", "happy as Larry", "on song", "a squiz", "up meself". "mate" recurs as the salutation, sign-off and greetings.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably Lardner's letter, misspellings kept: "appresiated", "that serious", "they excepted it".

engine.meaning: The story survives as most of it is verbatim, but a line is tacked on: "Your mate, JACK. Well, I'll be buggered." "I will make bloody good" also shifts the promise into bluster.
engine.sense: Mostly fits ("not skiting", "won't have sweet bugger-all on you"), but "the old bloke" for the manager loses "the old man" as the boss, and "not to be spooked of the high buildings" strains.
engine.authenticity: Swear words bolted onto otherwise unaltered prose: "all you bloody good old pals down home", "I will make bloody good", "this bloody big league business", and the tag "Well, I'll be buggered."
engine.register: Largely the original ("FRIEND AL: Well, Al old pal", "I will be perfectly satisfied") with "bloody" and "bugger" scattered heavier than a level-3 telling needs.
engine.tone: Jack's innocence wobbles under the oaths: "there won't be bugger all to it", and the closing exclamation reads like someone else talking.
engine.flow: Clunky where words were swapped in: "won't be bugger all to it", "I will make bloody good", "Your mate, JACK. Well, I'll be buggered."
engine.essence: Recognisably the original letter, misspellings kept: "Flynn misjuging that fly ball".

yarn.meaning: All points kept: the sale, the advice, the record, the scouting, the games, the homecoming. "gobsmacked" is colour on "dum".
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "won't be a patch on you" for won't have nothing on you, "never had Buckley's against me", "not skiting", "giving me the once-over", "not all up myself". "the fair go I got" for the treatment strains slightly.
yarn.authenticity: Natural: "it'll be dead easy", "happy as Larry", "spooked by the high buildings". A couple of stacked spots: "just dum, gobsmacked, couldn't say a word".
yarn.register: A light-to-middle weight that suits level 3, Jack's grammar kept and Aussie dropped in where it fits; no swearing.
yarn.tone: Keeps the naive boasting: "you know I am not skiting when I say that Al".
yarn.flow: Reads smoothly apart from the stacked "dum, gobsmacked,".
yarn.variety: Varied: "gobsmacked", "dead easy", "a patch on", "fair go", "skiting", "Buckley's", "happy as Larry", "beaut".
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the original, misspellings kept: "they excepted it", "I beat them twice in that serious."

unharnessed.why: An odd salutation; "mate" is spoken, not a letter heading.

engine.quote: Your mate, JACK. Well, I'll be buggered.
engine.why: A stock exclamation added after the signature; nothing in the letter calls for it.

engine.quote: all you bloody good old pals down home
engine.original: all you good old pals down home
engine.why: "bloody" stuffed into a warm line where it carries nothing.

engine.quote: not to be spooked of the high buildings
engine.original: not to be scared of the high buildings
engine.why: "spooked of" is ungrammatical; it is "spooked by".

yarn.quote: I was just dum, gobsmacked, couldn't say a word
yarn.original: I was just dum and couldn't say a word
yarn.why: Stacks a synonym onto the misspelled "dum".

yarn.quote: the fair go I got in Terre Haute
yarn.original: the treatment I got in Terre Haute
yarn.why: "fair go" is fair treatment as a principle; as "the treatment I got" it strains.

summaries.unharnessed: A natural, faithful retelling in Jack's voice, with the misspellings and the boasting intact.
summaries.engine: Mostly the original with "bloody" and "bugger" sprinkled in and an oath tacked on the end.
summaries.yarn: Faithful and natural at the right weight, with a couple of small strains.
